newsitem.title: DENMARK: Foreign buyers push Danish shares to record highs.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buyers push Danish shares to record highs.

text.p: Danish share prices closed at record highs on Tuesday, propelled by foreign buyers increasing their index portfolios at the half-year, dealers said.
"It is foreign investors placing index orders and as we are anyhow at such high levels, without very much paper in circulation, it is driving the index upward," a dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed up 2.92 point -- 1.7 percent -- at 174.63 in overall bourse turnover of 1.3 billion crowns.
The KFX August future rose 2.70 point to 174.70 with 60 contracts, each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Highest riser on the index was Sophus Berendsen.

It closed up 35.99 crowns, at 990.99, a 3.7 percent rise, bouncing back after Monday's 15 crown fall.Yesterday's fall and Tuesday's rally reflected movements in British-based Rentokil Initial, in which Sophus has a 35.8 percent stake.
On Tuesday it bought a Swedish laundry and Dutch linen supply firm.

Carlsberg, the only KFX share to fall, shed one crown to 365.00, its level before last week's British government decision to block the brewer's planned sale of its half of the Carlsberg-Tetley joint venture to partner Bass. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
